reauth_confirm.description: The {name} gateway {host} rejected the stored password. Enter the current OpenWebNet password.

init.title: Configuring {gateway}
init.description:
This is where the gateway is configured and where “basic” covers are calibrated - the ones whose position Home Assistant has to estimate from their run times.

**What you have to do**: pick one. Nothing changes until something is saved, and no cover moves before a screen says it is about to.

gateway.title: Gateway and connection
gateway.description: Where the gateway is, how it is spoken to, and where the configuration file lives. Saving reloads the integration with the new values.

data.generate_events: Generate events in Home Assistant for each message received

data_description.command_worker_count: How many command sessions the integration opens to the gateway. More sessions send queued commands in parallel, but gateways hold only a handful. Default 1 (1-4).
data_description.idle_watchdog_sec: No frame received on the monitor session for this long: a harmless probe is sent through the command session. Default 300 s (60-3600).
data_description.probe_window_sec: How long the probe is given to be answered. If nothing arrives on the monitor session and the gateway acknowledges no status request on the command session within this time, the connection is rebuilt. Default 30 s (5-300).
data_description.command_timeout_sec: How long a single command may take to be written and acknowledged before it is retried once and then dropped. Default 10 s (2-60).
data_description.queue_ttl_sec: Commands still queued after this long are dropped instead of being sent late. Default 60 s (10-600).
data_description.default_keepalive_minutes: Keep-alive requested from the energy meters when keepalive_minutes is set neither on the sensor nor in the gateway's sensor_defaults: block (alias energy:) of myhome.yaml. 0 disables it. Default 125 min (0-255).

profiles_covers.title: Profiles and covers
profiles_covers.description:
A **profile** describes one kind of cover: how long it takes to run, how long the slats take and how the curtain winds onto the roller. Every cover may follow one, and Home Assistant scales it to that cover's own height.

There are {profiles} profiles and {covers} basic covers on this gateway.

menu_options.pick_profile: View, edit or delete a profile

assign_covers.title: Which profile each cover follows
assign_covers.description:
**What is about to happen**: nothing moves. Assigning a profile means telling Home Assistant “this cover is built like those ones”, and the profile's values are scaled to this cover's height.

A profile does not beat what is written in the configuration file, if you use one: what always counts for most is what was measured on this cover itself.

**What you have to do**: pick a profile for each cover, or “No profile” to leave it on the file's values or the defaults.

assign_heights.title: How tall are these covers?
assign_heights.description:
A profile is the measurement of a cover of a certain height, and it is scaled to the others in proportion. The height of these is not known, so there is nothing to scale it by: {covers}.

**What you have to do**: measure, for each of them, the distance the bottom edge travels from fully closed to fully open, and write it in centimetres. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

pick_profile.title: Which profile?
pick_profile.description: **What you have to do**: pick the profile whose values you want to see or change. The next screen also lists the covers that follow it.

profile_actions.title: Profile “{profile}”
profile_actions.description:
Covers following it: {count}.

**What you have to do**: choose what to do with it. Viewing the values changes nothing; editing them or deleting the profile takes effect as soon as you close this dialog.

profile_view.title: Values of profile “{profile}”

profile_edit.title: Edit profile “{profile}”
profile_edit.description:
**What is about to happen**: the values below replace the measured ones, for every cover that follows this profile. Nothing moves: this is writing, not measuring.

**What you have to do**: correct what you know better than the calibration does - the run times from the manufacturer's sheet, for instance - and leave the rest alone. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

data_description.reference_height: The curtain travel of the cover this profile was measured on (20-500).
data_description.opening_time: Seconds from fully closed to fully open, slats included (1-600).
data_description.closing_time: Seconds from fully open to fully closed (1-600).
data_description.slat_time: Seconds the slats take to open before the curtain starts to rise (0-60).
data_description.opening_roll: How much the wound curtain speeds the ascent up: 1 is a bare tube, 2 a well-loaded one (1-5).

profile_delete.title: Delete profile “{profile}”?
profile_delete.description:
**What is about to happen**: the profile is deleted and these {count} covers go back to the values of the configuration file, if you use one, or to the defaults: {covers}

What was measured on each cover stays where it is: only the description of the kind is removed. If a profile of the same name exists in `cover_profiles:`, that one applies again from now on.

profile_deleted.title: Profile “{profile}” deleted
profile_deleted.description:
The profile is gone. Covers that followed it and went back to the file's values or to the defaults: {count} - {covers}

If that was a mistake, the way to rebuild it is to calibrate a cover of this kind again with the full measurement and give it the same name.

calibrations.title: Calibrations
calibrations.description:
These are the covers the integration keeps something of its own for: {count}. What is kept here beats the configuration file, if you use one.

**What you have to do**: pick the cover whose values you want to see, correct or delete.

no_calibrations.title: Nothing is stored yet
no_calibrations.description:
No cover of this gateway has values of its own kept by the integration: they all run on what the configuration file says, if you use one, or on the defaults.

**What you have to do**: go back to the menu and pick “Calibrate a cover” to measure one.

no_basic_covers.title: There is nothing to calibrate
no_basic_covers.description:
Every cover of this gateway reports its own position, so Home Assistant does not have to estimate it and there is no run time to measure.

The guided calibration is only for “basic” covers, the ones whose actuator does not say where it is.

calibration_actions.title: Calibration of {cover}

calibration_view.title: Values of {cover}

calibration_edit.title: Edit the values of {cover}
calibration_edit.description:
**What is about to happen**: the values below apply to this cover alone and beat both the profile and the configuration file. Nothing moves: this is writing, not measuring.

**What you have to do**: write only what you want to impose on this cover. A field left empty is not a zero: it means “I have nothing to say about this”, and the value goes back to coming from the profile or from the file. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

data_description.height: How far the bottom edge travels from fully closed to fully open (20-500).
data_description.opening_time: Seconds from fully closed to fully open, slats included (1-600).
data_description.closing_time: Seconds from fully open to fully closed (1-600).
data_description.slat_time: Seconds the slats take to open before the curtain starts to rise (0-60).
data_description.opening_roll: How much the wound curtain speeds the ascent up: 1 is a bare tube, 2 a well-loaded one (1-5).

calibration_delete.title: Delete the calibration of {cover}?
calibration_delete.description:
**What is about to happen**: the values kept for this cover are removed and the cover goes back to what the configuration file says, if you use one, or to the profile it follows.

The measurements cannot be recovered: getting them back means running the guided calibration again.

calibration_deleted.title: Calibration deleted
calibration_deleted.description: {cover} no longer has values of its own kept by the integration: it runs on what the configuration file says, if you use one, on the profile it follows, or on the defaults.

calibrate.title: Guided cover calibration
calibrate.description:
This tool calibrates “basic” covers: the ones whose actuator does not report its position. For those, the percentage you see in Home Assistant is an estimate computed from the run times; the calibration measures those times and the geometry of the roller, so that the estimate becomes a reliable one.

It will not be perfect. Expect a few centimetres out: 1-2 cm near the end stops, 2-4 cm between intermediate positions. Every full open or close re-synchronises the estimate, so the error does not build up.

“Advanced” covers report their position by themselves and need none of this, which is why they are not in the list.

**What is about to happen**: you will pick a cover and one of three ways of measuring it. The cover will run to its end stops several times.

**What you have to do**: keep a tape measure to hand, make sure nothing is in the cover's way, and stay where you can see it. Nothing is saved until the last screen: you can close this dialog whenever you like and nothing will have changed.

cover.title: Which cover are we measuring?
cover.description:
Only the “basic” covers of this gateway are listed: the ones that do not report their own position and are therefore the only ones it makes sense to calibrate with this tool.

**Which one to pick**: if this is the first time, pick a cover that is representative of its kind and easy to measure - one you can stand in front of without moving furniture, whose bottom edge a tape measure reaches. What is measured on this one will hold for every cover like it.

**What you have to do**: go and stand in front of the cover you have chosen, with this tool to hand (your phone or your laptop), and then confirm it below. You will be asked to watch it move and to measure it with a tape, so you have to be physically next to the cover you choose.

path.title: How do you want to measure {cover}?
path.description:
There are three ways, and the right one depends on what you have measured already. They are not steps in a sequence: you pick one.

The first (A) is the long one, about three minutes: three button presses and three tape readings. It ends in a **profile**, the description of this kind of cover, which every similar cover (same model, same size, ...) can then reuse.

The second (B) is meant precisely for covers similar to one already calibrated: pick the profile, measure the height, done.

The third (C) is for a cover that follows a profile and keeps stopping in the wrong place.

**What you have to do**: pick one of the ways below. Nothing moves until the next screen.

menu_options.path_a: (A) It is the first cover of its kind (full measurement, ~3 minutes)
menu_options.path_b: (B) It is similar to a cover already measured (height only)
menu_options.path_c: (C) It follows a profile but stops in the wrong place (refine it)

path_a.title: Before {cover} starts moving
path_a.description:
**What is about to happen**: the cover will close completely, then open completely, then close again, and finally stop somewhere in between. Seven movements in all, about three minutes.

**What you have to do**: make sure nothing is in the way - open windows, plants on the sill, cats - and keep the tape measure to hand. You will be asked to press a button when something happens, and to read a few distances.

Two of the steps ask you to be quick and precise, but the instructions always come before the movement and you are the one who starts it. You can stop whenever you like: nothing is saved until the last screen, and the movements are ordinary commands.

path_b.title: What kind of cover is {cover}?
path_b.description:
A profile describes a model of cover: how long it takes to run, how long the slats take and how the curtain winds onto the roller. Home Assistant scales it to this cover as soon as it knows how tall it is.

**What you have to do**: pick the profile measured on a cover similar to this one. On the next screen you will measure the height of this one.

path_c.title: Refine {cover}
path_c.description:
This cover follows a profile and does not behave like it: the motor may be slower, the curtain heavier, the roller thicker. What you measure here applies to this cover alone and beats both the profile and the configuration file, if you use one; everything you do not measure goes on coming from the profile.

**What you have to do**: confirm which profile this cover should start from.

refine_scope.title: How far do you want to refine {cover}?
refine_scope.description:
**What is about to happen**: either two measured runs (one up and one down), or those plus two tape readings.

The times alone are enough for a cover whose motor is simply slower or faster than the one the profile was measured on. Add the coefficients when it is wrong *half way* as well: there it is not the motor that turns differently, it is the curtain that winds differently.

**What you have to do**: choose how far to go. You can always come back and do the rest.

menu_options.times_only: Its own run times only (2 presses, ~1 minute)
menu_options.times_and_rolls: Its own times and its own coefficients (2 presses and 2 readings)

home_closed_done.title: Is {cover} completely closed?
home_closed_done.description:
**What happened**: the cover was sent all the way down, so that everything measured from here on starts from a known point.

**What you have to do**: look at it. If it is completely closed, slats shut and the bottom edge resting, go on. If it is still moving, wait and then go on. If it did not move at all, or moved the wrong way, say so below.

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

home_open_done.title: Is {cover} completely open?
home_open_done.description:
**What happened**: the cover was sent all the way up, because what follows runs down from there and a run that started anywhere else would measure nothing.

**What you have to do**: look at it. If it is completely open, go on. If it is still moving, wait and then go on. If it did not move at all, or moved the wrong way, say so below.

menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_brief.title: We are about to measure {cover} going up
open_brief.description:
**What is about to happen**: when you press the button below, the cover starts upwards from the bottom. For the first second or two only the slats open, while the bottom edge stays on its rest; then the whole curtain starts to rise, and at the top the cover stops by itself.

**What you have to do**: here you will have to be quick and precise. You will be asked for two presses, one after the other: the first at the instant the bottom edge leaves its rest, the second at the instant the cover stops at the top. You are not timing anything - the instant of the press is the measurement.

Read this at your own pace, get into position, and start the movement yourself when you are ready.

open_lift.title: {cover} is opening
open_lift.description:
**What is happening**: the cover has started to rise. Right now the slats are opening and the bottom edge is still on its rest.

**What you have to do**: watch the bottom edge and press the button below **at the instant it leaves its rest**. Then let the cover carry on: it will reach the top by itself and you will be asked for the second press.

menu_options.lifted_off: 2) Press at the instant it leaves its rest
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_top.title: {cover} is still rising
open_top.description:
**What is happening**: the curtain is winding on and the cover will stop by itself at the top.

**What you have to do**: press the button below **at the instant it reaches the end stop and the motor stops**. If you missed the moment, repeat the step rather than guessing: the whole opening time comes from this press.

menu_options.stopped_open: 3) Press at the instant it stops at the end
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

open_result.title: {cover} going up: {run} s
open_result.description:
**What was measured**: slats {slat} s, full ascent {run} s.

**What you have to do**: if both presses felt right, go on. If either was late or early, repeat the measurement: the cover is sent back down and the ascent is run again. A press half a second out moves the estimate by a few centimetres.

close_brief.title: We are about to measure {cover} going down
close_brief.description:
**What is about to happen**: when you press the button below, the cover starts downwards from the top and stops by itself once the curtain is down and the slats have closed.

**What you have to do**: here too you will have to be quick and precise, but this time there is only one press, at the instant the cover stops at the bottom. A cover comes down a little faster than it goes up, which is why this is measured separately.

Read this at your own pace, get into position, and start the movement yourself when you are ready.

close_bottom.title: {cover} is closing
close_bottom.description:
**What is happening**: the cover is coming down and will stop by itself once the curtain is down and the slats have closed.

**What you have to do**: press the button below **at the instant it reaches the end stop and the motor stops**. That press is the whole closing time.

menu_options.stopped_closed: 2) Press at the instant it stops at the end
menu_options.not_right: It did not do what it should

close_result.title: {cover} going down: {run} s
close_result.description:
**What was measured**: full descent {run} s.

**What you have to do**: if the press felt right, go on. Otherwise repeat the measurement: the cover is sent back up and the descent is run again.

height.title: How tall is {cover}?
height.description:
**What you have to do**: with the cover completely open, measure from the point where the bottom edge rests when it is closed (the base) up to the bottom edge where it is now. In other words, measure the distance the cover travels from fully open to fully closed (or the other way round), and write the centimetres below.

That distance is the curtain travel, and it is the reference every other measurement is compared against. Measure the curtain, not the window: if the bottom edge rests on a sill rather than on the floor, measure from the sill.

data_description.height: In centimetres. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point: 198,5 or 198.5.

height_result.title: Curtain travel of {cover}: {height} cm
height_result.description:
**What was written down**: {height} cm from the base to the bottom edge with the cover completely open.

**What you have to do**: if that is the number you read off the tape, go on. It is the measurement every other one is referred to, so it is worth checking.

measure_descent.title: Measure {cover} - {percent}% of the way down
measure_descent.description:
**What happened**: the cover was opened completely and then run down {percent}% of its travel.

**What you have to do**: measure again from the base up to the bottom edge where it is now, and write the centimetres below. The same reference as the height, so that the two measurements can be compared.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; within {tolerance} cm is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

measure_ascent.title: Measure {cover} - {percent}% of the way up
measure_ascent.description:
**What happened**: the cover was closed completely and then run up through the slats plus {percent}% of its travel.

**What you have to do**: measure from the base up to the bottom edge where it is now, and write the centimetres below. A cover is not loaded the same way going up and going down, which is why the same fraction is measured twice.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; within {tolerance} cm is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

measure_verify.title: Check {cover} - {percent}% of the way down
measure_verify.description:
**What happened**: the cover was taken to a position nothing was measured at, so this is a real check and not a repetition.

**What you have to do**: measure the height of the bottom edge one last time, from the same reference as before, and write the centimetres below. The next screen says how far the cover is from where Home Assistant believed it to be.

data_description.measured_cm: About {expected} cm is expected; within {tolerance} cm is perfectly normal. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point.

tape_result.title: {measured} cm read at {percent}%
tape_result.description:
**What was written down**: {measured} cm from the base to the bottom edge.

**What you have to do**: if that is the number you read off the tape, go on. If you suspect you measured from the wrong point, repeat the measurement: the cover goes back to its end stop and runs the same distance again, so the reading can be taken under the same conditions.

verify_offer.title: Do you want to check {cover}?
verify_offer.description:
The height was all that was needed: the calibration can be saved as it is.

**What the check is**: the cover is sent half way and you measure where it really stopped, which says whether this cover really behaves like the profile. It takes about a minute and one tape reading.

verify_result.title: {cover} stopped {deviation} cm from the estimate
verify_result.description:
That is the distance between where the cover really stopped and where Home Assistant believed it would. One or two centimetres are normal and already a very good approximation; three or more mean that this cover does not behave like the profile it was given.

**What you have to do**: go on, or repeat the measurement if you think the reading was wrong. If it appears, the refinement measures this cover on its own.

menu_options.path_c: Refine this cover with its own measurements

profile_name.title: Name this kind of cover
profile_name.description:
{cover} has been measured, and what was measured describes every cover similar to it. Give that kind a name and the others will be calibrated in two screens instead of ten.

**What you have to do**: write a short name - letters, digits and underscores only, no spaces and no accents, because it is also a key of the configuration file. Something like `tall`, `bedrooms` or `kitchen_door`.

The name is asked for now because it appears in the summary on the next screen. A name already in use is not refused: the profile of that name is **replaced** by the one just measured, and that is how a cover whose first measurement went badly is measured again. A `cover_profiles:` block of the same name in the configuration file is left untouched and goes on sitting behind the measured one.

summary_basic.title: What was measured on {cover}

menu_options.refine: Improve the accuracy (~2 minutes, 4 more readings)

summary_precise.title: What was measured on {cover}
summary_precise.description:
**Curtain travel**: {height}
**Accuracy**: within {accuracy}, checked at {percent}%

The accuracy is the distance between where the model puts the bottom edge and where the tape really found it, measured at a position nothing was fitted to.

**Where these values go**: if you save, they stay inside Home Assistant, here under Configure → Calibrations, and the cover uses them at once instead of the ones in the configuration file, if you use one. From that same screen you can look at them again, correct them by hand or delete them at any time.

If you would rather write them into the file yourself, the equivalent snippet is below: copy it before you close this, because without saving nothing is kept.

{yaml}
**What you have to do**: save.

saved.title: Calibration of {cover} saved
saved.description:
Done: the calibration of {cover} is saved and already in use. From now on {cover} moves on the values just measured; you will find them among the entity's attributes, marked “guided”.

**Where to find it again**: here under Configure → Calibrations, and the profile “{profile}” under Configure → Profiles and covers. If one day you want the values written in the configuration file back, all you have to do is delete the calibration from that screen.

**What you can do now**: calibrate another cover, or close. Every cover similar to this one takes two screens, by choosing “(B) It is similar to a cover already measured”.

cancelled.title: Calibration cancelled
cancelled.description: Nothing was saved. The cover is where the last movement left it and goes on moving as it did before.

expired.title: The session expired through inactivity
expired.description:
This calibration stood still for too long, so {cover} was released: it is no longer being calibrated and answers ordinary commands again.

**Nothing was saved**, and the cover is where the last movement left it. The measurements taken so far were discarded: getting them back means starting again from the beginning.

refused_unknown_cover.title: That cover is not there any more
refused_unknown_cover.description:
The cover is no longer part of this gateway's configuration, so there is nothing to measure. Nothing was saved.

If you renamed or moved it in the configuration file, reload the integration and try again.

refused_already_calibrating.title: This cover is already being calibrated
refused_already_calibrating.description:
There is another dialog open on this cover, or the `cover_calibration_run` service is driving it. Two calibrations on the same motor would each measure a run the other one stopped, so this one was not started.

**What you have to do**: finish or close the other one, then try again.

problem_no_echo.title: {cover} did not answer
problem_no_echo.description:
The command reached the bus but the actuator never reported that it had started moving, so there is no instant to measure against and the step was abandoned.

**The cover may still be moving**: the command really did go out, so the motor most likely started. A stop was sent straight after the failure, but if the cover is still running, stop it yourself before repeating the step.

**What you have to do**: check that the cover is not jammed, that nobody else (a wall switch, an automation) is holding it, and repeat the step. If it happens every time, this actuator does not report its own state and the guided calibration cannot measure it.

problem_not_delivered.title: The command never reached the bus
problem_not_delivered.description:
The gateway neither wrote our command nor said it had given up on it, so {cover} was never asked to move and nothing was measured.

**What you have to do**: check that the gateway is connected - the integration page says so - and repeat the step.

problem_not_stopped.title: {cover} could not be stopped
problem_not_stopped.description:
The stop command was refused or lost, so the cover carried on to its end stop and the position this step was about does not exist.

**What you have to do**: wait for the cover to be still and repeat the step. This usually happens with a gateway that is busy with a great many commands.

problem_busy.title: {cover} is already moving
problem_busy.description:
A step has to start from a standstill, and this cover was already moving - somebody at a wall switch, an automation, or a command that had not finished.

**What you have to do**: wait for it to stop, then repeat the step.

problem_bad_point.title: Those two presses cannot both be right
problem_bad_point.description:
The instants do not hold together: the cover cannot have stopped before it started, nor opened its slats after arriving.

**What you have to do**: repeat the step and press once for each event, at the moment it happens.

problem_timeout.title: Nothing was pressed in time
problem_timeout.description:
This screen waits about a minute and a half for the press it is about, far longer than any cover takes to run. Past that limit the press no longer measures anything, so it was discarded rather than believed.

**What you have to do**: repeat the step and this time press as soon as the cover does what the screen describes.

problem_unknown.title: Something went wrong with {cover}
problem_unknown.description:
The step did not finish and nothing was measured. The detail is in the Home Assistant log.

**What you have to do**: repeat the step. Whatever you choose, nothing has been saved.

progress.homing_closed: {cover} is being closed completely, so that the measurements start from a known point. Please wait, and make sure nothing is in the way.
progress.homing_open: {cover} is being opened completely, so that the next movement starts from a known point. Please wait, and make sure nothing is in the way.
progress.starting_open: {cover} is starting upwards. Watch it: in a moment you will be asked for the first press.
progress.starting_close: {cover} is starting downwards. Watch it: in a moment you will be asked for the press.
progress.running_down: {cover} is being opened completely and then run down to about {percent}% of its travel. Please wait, and have the tape measure ready.
progress.running_up: {cover} is being closed completely and then run up to about {percent}% of its travel. Please wait, and have the tape measure ready.

error.invalid_host: Not a valid IP address or hostname.
error.invalid_config_path: There is no readable file at this path.
error.not_a_number: Write a number. Decimals may be written with a comma or with a point: 198,5 or 198.5.
error.out_of_range: The number is outside the range this field accepts.
error.above_the_travel: That is more than the whole travel of this curtain. Measure from the point where the bottom edge rests when the cover is closed, not from the floor.
error.invalid_name: A profile name may only contain letters, digits and underscores: no spaces, no accents, no hyphens.

options.__none__: No profile (the file's values, or the defaults)

yaml_invalid.title: MyHOME configuration file is invalid
yaml_invalid.description:
The integration could not load `{path}`:

```
{message}
```

Fix the file and reload the MyHOME integration. No device is created until the file is valid.

unknown_keys.title: Unknown keys in the MyHOME configuration file

no_devices_for_gateway.title: No devices configured for this MyHOME gateway
no_devices_for_gateway.description:
Gateway `{mac}` has no section in `{path}` (gateways found in the file: {others}), so no device was created.

Add a section for this gateway, or check that the MAC address matches, then reload the integration.

gateway_required.message: Specify the gateway: {count} gateways are loaded.

sync_time.description: Synchronizes the gateway clock with the Home Assistant local time.

gateway.name: Gateway

send_message.name: Send message
send_message.description: Sends an arbitrary (but valid) OpenWebNet message to the gateway.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

start_sending_instant_power.name: Start sending instant power
start_sending_instant_power.description: Asks the energy meter of the targeted power sensors to send instant power updates.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: For how many minutes (1-255) the instant power updates are sent. Defaults to the sensor's keepalive_minutes.

start_discovery.name: Start device discovery
start_discovery.description: Listens to the bus for 60 seconds and writes YAML suggestions for unknown devices to myhome_discovered.yaml.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

stop_discovery.name: Stop device discovery
stop_discovery.description: Stops a running device discovery and writes the suggestions collected so far.

gateway.name: Gateway
gateway.description: MAC address of the gateway. Optional when only one gateway is configured.

cover_calibration_run.name: Calibrate cover (run)
cover_calibration_run.description: Sends the cover to one end, then runs it for exactly the motor time a set_cover_position 50 would use with its current configuration and stops it there, so the height of the bar can be measured for cover_calibration_compute.

direction.name: Direction
direction.description: Which run to measure: 'close' starts from fully open and runs half the curtain time, 'open' starts from fully closed and runs the slat time plus half the curtain time.

cover_calibration_compute.name: Calibrate cover (compute)
cover_calibration_compute.description: Turns the heights measured after cover_calibration_run into the roll of this cover - one per direction when both runs were measured - and returns a cover_profiles snippet ready to paste into myhome.yaml.

height.name: Curtain travel
height.description: Distance in centimetres between the fully open and the fully closed bar (the travel, not the window).

closed_half_cm.name: Height after the closing half run
closed_half_cm.description: Centimetres between the floor and the bottom of the bar, measured after cover_calibration_run with direction 'close'.

opened_half_cm.name: Height after the opening half run
opened_half_cm.description: The same measurement after direction 'open'. Optional: it is what gives the separate opening_roll, and without it only the closing roll is worked out.

slat_time.name: Slat time
slat_time.description: Seconds of slat-only travel. It is an input, never an answer: given here it is used as it stands, otherwise the value configured on the cover is.

closed_run_seconds.name: Closing run length
closed_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the closing run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.

opened_run_seconds.name: Opening run length
opened_run_seconds.description: Motor seconds the opening run really lasted, as reported by cover_calibration_run. Only needed when the cover's times changed in between: it defaults to the same value the run computed.
